notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR3: "Identifier-3 must reference an integer data item." CommunicationBinder#ScreenSendAdvancing refuses (COBOL6171) an operand IsIntegerItem rejects; probes at --std 85 accept and run PIC 9, S9(3) holding -1, 9(18) holding 0 and all nines, BINARY, PACKED-DECIMAL, COMP, 9PP, a subscripted and a qualified item and LINAGE-COUNTER, and refuse P9, 9V9, X, ZZ9, a group, a USAGE INDEX item, an index-name, a symbolic-character and FUNCTION INTEGER (an integer function "may be used only in an arithmetic expression", §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4) (classes b, d, f). One shape under-rejects: a reference-modified integer item (N18 (1:2), N2 (2:1)) is accepted, though reference modification of a numeric item yields a data item of class and category alphanumeric (§1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5), because IsIntegerItem reads the base item's PicInfo through the RefModPlace. No kb/Work note holds it (PB5289 landed the 9PP, index and symbolic-character arms). kb/Work PB5384 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-reread2/rr-07.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Identifier-3 must reference an integer data item."; 2023: "2023 SEND (14.9.38) sends to a message server via literal-1/identifier-1; it has no ADVANCING phrase and no identifier-3 operand". The 1985 SEND identifier-3 is the ADVANCING line count of the communication module. 2023's SEND is a message-server statement with no advancing operand. WRITE's similar rule belongs to another statement.
